web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Nine Years of Numbers—Where the Compounding Slowed
question: What do Protean's multi-year financial statements reveal about growth quality, margin compression, cash conversion, and capital efficiency?

epigraph.quote: Sales grew at 10.6% over five years, ROE sits at 10.0%, and earnings include ₹68 crore of other income.
epigraph.author: Audited Consolidated Financial Forensics

web_blocks.title: Multi-Year Profit & Loss: Growth Without Operating Leverage

web_blocks.html: From FY18 (₹898 crore) to FY26 (₹998 crore), Protean's sales grew just 11.1% in total [1]. Sales dipped during FY19–FY21 (₹603 crore) before a post-COVID rebound [1]. Five-year sales growth sits at 10.6% CAGR [1]. More worrying for owners is steady margin drop. Operating margin (OPM) peaked at 23% in FY19 (₹177 crore profit on ₹755 crore sales) [1]. It slid to 16% in FY23 and settled at 10–12% across FY24–FY26 [1]. On a TTM basis through September 2026, sales reached ₹1,058 crore [1]. Yet operating profit was just ₹107 crore (10.1% OPM), and net profit fell to ₹75 crore as depreciation hit ₹62 crore [1].

web_blocks.caption: Protean eGov Consolidated Profit & Loss (FY18–TTM Sep 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue reached a record ₹998 Cr in FY26 (₹1,058 Cr TTM), but OPM halved from 23% in FY19 to 10–12%, leaving TTM PAT (₹75 Cr) well below FY18 (₹136 Cr).

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet & Cash Flow Forensics: Surplus Cash vs. Rising Asset Intensity

web_blocks.html: Protean's balance sheet stays safe on debt [1, 13]. Borrowings were ₹87 crore in FY26 and ₹128 crore in September 2026, mostly lease dues under Ind AS 116 [1, 13]. That sits against ₹1,078 crore of equity and reserves, plus over ₹800 crore in cash and investments [1, 13]. However, asset intensity is climbing fast. Fixed assets plus CWIP jumped from ₹74 crore in FY23 to ₹186 crore in FY26 [1, 16]. By September 2026, that figure hit ₹325 crore as ASK fit-outs and software spend accelerated [1, 16].

web_blocks.caption: Protean eGov Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY18–Sep 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Net worth stands at ₹1,064 Cr (Sep 2026) with ~₹506+ Cr in investments, but Fixed Assets + CWIP more than quadrupled from ₹74 Cr (FY23) to ₹325 Cr (Sep 2026).

web_blocks.html: Cash conversion has been uneven. Across FY18–FY26, total CFO was ₹847 crore against ₹1,015 crore of total PAT—an 83% ratio [1]. Working-capital swings hurt CFO in FY22 (₹11 crore), FY24 (₹58 crore), and FY26 (₹78 crore vs ₹101 crore PAT) [1]. Free cash flow in FY26 shrank to ₹12 crore after ₹66 crore of capex [1]. In November 2026, an adverse GST appeal upheld a ₹5.65 crore penalty plus ₹2.34 crore interest [17]. That ruling added to contingent tax claims [17].

Capital allocation also merits close watch. Protean paid ₹10 per share in annual dividends across FY24, FY25, and FY26 (~₹40 crore per year) [1, 19]. In FY26, that ₹40 crore payout exceeded ₹12 crore of Free Cash Flow by ₹28 crore [1]. The firm funded the gap from its ₹800+ crore cash reserve [1]. That buffer keeps the dividend safe today, yet sustained capex will slowly trim treasury interest income.

web_blocks.caption: Protean eGov Consolidated Cash Flows (FY18–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: FY26 CFO fell to ₹78 Cr (from ₹193 Cr in FY25) and capex consumed ₹66 Cr, leaving just ₹12 Cr in Free Cash Flow.

web_blocks.caption: Protean eGov Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY18–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE compressed from 22% (FY20) to 13% (FY26) and ROE sits at 10.0%, weighed down by low-yielding treasury cash and rising capex.

web_blocks.title: Why ROE Sits at 10.0% Despite Zero Debt
paragraphs: Holding ~₹800 crore of cash and investments earning ~7–8% pre-tax drags ROE down to 10.0% and ROCE to 12.7% [1].
Even after removing surplus cash, core margins (10–12% OPM) no longer match the high returns of FY19–FY20.

book_paragraphs: Numbers strip away narratives. When you line up Protean's consolidated financial statements from FY18 through the trailing twelve months ended September 2026, you see a business that has grown its top line modestly while losing half of its operating margin. Revenue moved from ₹898 crore in FY18 to ₹998 crore in FY26 and ₹1,058 crore on a trailing basis—a five-year sales compound growth rate of 10.6 percent. Yet operating profit moved in the opposite direction, falling from ₹181 crore in FY18 to ₹116 crore in FY26 and ₹107 crore over the last twelve months.

Why did operating margins compress from 23 percent in FY19 to 10 to 12 percent today? Three forces converged. First, employee expenses and technology investments climbed steadily as Protean built new digital stacks ahead of revenue. Second, identity verification pricing faced fierce competition. Third, the mix shifted toward lower-margin RFP and physical facilitation work. On a trailing twelve-month basis, net profit sits at ₹75 crore—nearly 45 percent below the ₹136 crore Protean earned back in FY18.

The balance sheet tells a story of safety colliding with rising capital intensity. Protean carries virtually no financial debt—its ₹128 crore of borrowings in September 2026 largely reflects lease liabilities—and holds more than ₹800 crore in cash and liquid investments. That cash pile is both a cushion and a mask. It earned ₹68 crore in other income in FY26, cushioning pre-tax profit, while simultaneously depressing return on equity to 10.0 percent and return on capital employed to 12.7 percent. Worse, fixed assets and capital work-in-progress surged from ₹74 crore in FY23 to ₹325 crore by September 2026 as Aadhaar Seva Kendra fit-outs and capitalized software piled onto the books.

Cash conversion confirms that Protean is in an investment-heavy phase. Operating cash flow dropped from ₹193 crore in FY25 to ₹78 crore in FY26, and ₹66 crore of capital expenditure left just ₹12 crore in free cash flow. Add a November 2026 adverse GST appellate ruling upholding ₹5.65 crore in penalties plus ₹2.34 crore in interest, and the forensic picture is clear: Protean is financially rock-solid on solvency, yet its core operating engine is currently generating sub-cost-of-capital returns while awaiting payoff from its new DPI investments.

Ten years of financial statements rarely lie. Looking across FY17 to FY26, Protean's revenue compounded at a modest 10.6% five-year pace, while operating profit margins compressed from 23% in FY19 to 11% in FY26. Return on equity sits at 10.0%, below the cost of equity for Indian small-and-mid-cap technology businesses. Until Fixed Assets and CWIP (now ₹325 Cr) begin generating high-margin cash flows rather than absorbing them, earnings quality remains heavily reliant on treasury interest.

Cash conversion is ultimately where accounting meets reality. Between FY23 and H1 FY27, Protean's Fixed Assets and Capital Work-in-Progress expanded more than fourfold from ₹74 Cr to ₹325 Cr, while consolidated ROE hovered at 10.0%. Until those newly capitalized assets begin throwing off steady operating cash flow above ₹140 Cr annually, the financial statements point to a capital-absorbing transition rather than an asset-light compounder.
That completes our price-blind business and forensic audit. With CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality locked in, Chapter 7 finally opens the market price to see what ₹705.60 assumes.

book_callouts.title: The Forensic Bottom Line Before Price
book_callouts.text: Before ever looking at a stock chart or valuation multiple, ask yourself what kind of business Protean is today. It is a debt-free, cash-rich sovereign infrastructure operator with a 97 percent pension moat, a threatened 50 percent tax-processing leg, and a 10 percent ROE. Whether that makes an attractive investment depends entirely on what price the market demands for that transition risk.

book_subsections.title: Deconstructing Return on Capital
paragraphs: A common mistake is to dismiss Protean's 10 percent ROE as merely a cash-drag artifact. True, holding ₹800 crore in treasury investments earning 7 to 8 percent dilutes headline ROE. Yet even if you strip out treasury cash and other income, core operating profit after depreciation in FY26 was only ₹62 crore before tax—roughly ₹47 crore after tax—against an operating capital base that has now swelled past ₹325 crore in fixed assets plus working capital. Until operating margins recover toward 16 to 18 percent, core return on invested capital remains pedestrian.

book_subsections.title: Bridging to Valuation and Market Expectations
paragraphs: With the price-blind business and forensic audit complete, the central analytical question shifts to price. An asset-heavy transition with 10 percent ROE and a looming PAN 2.0 tender cliff requires a very different margin of safety than an asset-light 25 percent ROE compounder. Chapter 7 will test what growth and margin recovery the market is currently pricing into Protean's shares.
